translations.text: An exposition that he delivered one day when he saw the crowd attached to the man who deserved a curse. He wanted them to tell that man what he repeatedly said about him, and he wanted the others to guard themselves against that man's deeds.
God says in the scriptures that belong to him, “Children shall not die for their fathers,” and, “The fathers shall not eat sour grapes and the children's teeth be set on edge.”
Likewise, no faithful slave will die for unbelieving masters. Nor will the ungodliness of godless masters who worship trees and stones come upon slaves whose hope is in God and his Christ, Jesus.
The negligence of unbelieving and oppressive masters will come upon them, and the righteousness of faithful slaves will come upon them.
There is no slavery in the place where we are going, for those who will now free themselves from slavery to sin.
Since each person will give an account of himself to God, listen to what is written: “Separate yourselves! Separate yourselves! Do not touch anything unclean!”

Do not share in the deeds of those who are slaves of Cronus, who love Hecate and are mad about her, gazing into her face, her prostitute’s appearance, lest Jesus, who hates those people, hate you along with them.
And the holy Scripture said that the angels spoke with Lot to make him leave Sodom quickly, warning him not to perish along with them.
They are now saying to you too, O human being, through the word of God, that you should separate yourself from their sins, lest he make you like them and wipe you out along with them.

There is a reckless weakness into which someone may fall: that people like us, who say, “We love the one who gave us knowledge, Christ,” should accept a gift of anything at all from godless people, or instead send them gifts, establishing a friendship for ourselves with the enemies of Christ.

They openly reveal to our people, or to crowds of people, that they are idol worshipers, bowing down to these images of demons and saying in their insolence, “Just as we cannot change you into pagans, you cannot change us into Christians.”

For whoever bows down to godless people bows down to the one who dwells in them, the devil, and honors the one they serve, the serpent. But whoever bows down to people of God bows down to God who dwells in them and honors the one they serve, Jesus.
If you say, “The Lord welcomes sinners and eats with them,” then consider why he does so: so that they will believe in him, or so that they will blaspheme him?
Or if he was not going to benefit them, how could he say, “I have come to call sinners to repentance”?
Or do you not see the sign of their willingness toward the one who called them? It is this: all the tax collectors and sinners were drawing near to him to listen to him.
If you invite an unbeliever and he comes to your God’s dinner and eats from the good things of which he said, “I have prepared them,” then that is good.
If an unbeliever invites you to dinner, you too may eat with him, as your Lord Jesus did. Your cup is separate from that of the [?]
[?] of the hands that are stretched out away from [?].
They used to thresh grain when it had more chaff or was very full.
Why should I be afraid of foolish people?
They are not ashamed to say, “There is no God.”
The lawlessness of pagans will surround me—those who trust in their wealth and boast of empty hopes.

If from the beginning they have spread bad reports about the people of God, as it is written, it has also been said, “The righteous person will be remembered forever. He will not be afraid of bad news.”
What will the enemies of Christ say against me, except to pour lies out of their mouths against me about all sorts of things that never happened?
As someone said, whether he was sincere or not: “When they speak against you in the houses of the rich, I tell them what is good about you.”
For before all people who hope in Jesus, there is openness toward me on their part, and only [?] toward me.
But those rich oppressors have nothing to say against me except, “You turn the hearts of the poor away from us, so that they will not do forced labor in gardens or in any work beyond their strength.”
And they say, “He openly entered our houses and carried away the things we worship, to our shame, because we could not stop him.”
For what other punishment and what other scourge is not upon godless people, without their noticing it?
Or is this great wrath upon them not enough—that they do not know God?
But do not let any of us think this: “If only God would repay with evil those who insult us!”
Remember, then, the Lord’s patience: he did not make the tongues of those who cursed him split apart in their mouths.

And he did not make those who crucified him split apart down the middle, just as he has not torn out the tongues of those who blaspheme him now, nor made the flesh of those who say, “He is not God,” fall away.
But they will indeed fall apart and split open, and their tongues will split and be torn out when the Lord Jesus shows them the day of their slaughter.
It is indeed laid down that God’s people should pray for those who persecute them.
For this reason we bless those who curse us, in accordance with the commandment of our teacher and Lord, Christ.
For if his disciples and his servants curse people because they speak evil of them, they bear guilt toward them.

But if they do not curse those people for uttering this abomination with their mouths—that the true God alone, the Father of our Lord Jesus, is not God—they share with them in their deeds and their words.
And they share with them in their deeds and their words.
And they are liable along with them to their judgment and their curse, and to wrath and Gehenna.
If, then, these people, who have gone beyond the nature of animals, have not known God and have not understood his wonders, his powers, and all his works—
not only those on earth, which they see and hear about, but also those in heaven and everything he will do—
how will they know his people and their deeds?
Is the person who fears a mortal human being, and a son of man who withers like grass, not a laughingstock to little children without understanding, who jump and tremble when
they hear the sound of foxes or see them?

But they can find nothing against you except this alone: the judgments concerning fighting against them, and justice in every matter, and especially your keeping away from Christ’s enemies and those who oppress the poor.
For the evil words that their offspring speak against us are no worse than those their father speaks about those who fight against his thoughts at all times.
And what, then, are the good words that some people will speak to us? They are no better than those Jesus, our king and our Lord, speaks into our hearts at all times.
Nor is the struggle against those who oppose us greater than the struggle against their father, the devil, against whom we fight at all times.
If the help of brothers and friends who help one another is good—for it is good when people find faithful friends and true brothers—God’s help is greater than all these.
For this reason, these people and those others are not my concern.
Did not a governor [?], a pagan governor, dare to say, when he came here, “I really marvel that you are cheerful”?
I answered him like this: “Why should someone who has no God but Jesus not be cheerful?
Do we worship handmade idols of demons?
As the prophets said about them, ‘There is no joy for the ungodly, says the Lord God.’”

Nevertheless, woe to you, woe to you, assembly of calves and dogs and every beast of creation, from which God’s anger has not withdrawn to this day and will not withdraw until the end, for it is indeed an assembly of wicked people.
But a gathering of calves in a street surrounded me and seized me.
The ingratitude is not hidden from Jesus, nor has he forgotten it, because they insult him and his saints within it or through them.

For they have already explained their name: “The woman filled with demons, whom every evil spirit has defiled so that they may satisfy their desires with her.” And she belongs to them, the partner of those who blaspheme God,
rejoicing over them on the day of their rebuke,
or laughing with those who laugh at you,
because they insult God and revile his saints while you listen.
For they do not blaspheme God and his people in private rooms, but in marketplaces and in streets where there are many listeners.
I too tell you openly, in the midst of this crowd, so that the districts and the whole land may hear these words:
Cursed are those who say, “People used to [?] gods,” or, “Gods die.”
Cursed are those who say, “If God is a god, why did he not know where the devil had come from?”
They said this because they heard in Job that the King, God Almighty, asked that demon, “Where have you come from?”
They did not understand the meaning of what they heard, for God has spoken in the Scriptures on many occasions.
For if those godless people had understood, would they not have realized that people customarily threaten servants [?] and say, “Where are you coming from?” even when they know?
Just as Elisha questioned Gehazi, knowing where he had come from and what he had done, so the Lord questioned the devil threateningly:
“Where are you coming from, destroyer, liar, you who boast over weak people?
Have you then paid attention, weakling, to my servant Job? There is no one like him.
If you want to fight, advance against him.

For I have tolerated you, demon, as a test for my chosen ones, so that they may laugh at you because of all the humiliation you suffer at their hands when they defeat you—you angel who is killed, you lion and dragon who is trampled by those whom I have granted to gird with strength and to gird with power to oppose your [?] acts of impiety.”
Cursed are those who say, “If he is a god, why did he not know where Adam was?”
For they said this because they heard in Genesis, “Adam, where are you?”
They do not know that a question may concern not hidden matters but things that are apparent and known, just as God asked Moses, “What is that in your hand?” and Moses acknowledged, “It is a staff.”
And just as Joseph questioned his brothers, “Who are you, and where are you from?” although he was not ignorant.
For if they had understood, they would have shut their mouths and refrained from saying these impious things—that breed of people who themselves said from the beginning, “How did God know?”
And, “Is there knowledge in the Most High?”
Those who say, “If Jesus is God, why did he not know where they had put Lazarus?” are cursed.
They said this because they heard in the Gospel, “Where have you put him?”
They do not know that the Lord asked as a human being, although he is God, and that this kind of expression often occurs in conversations, especially those of human beings.
As he said, or as the Lord himself did this as a man, as it is written in Genesis, when he asked Abraham, “Where is Sarah your wife?”
Just as the angel also asked the women in the tomb, “Who are you looking for?”
The Lord also did this when he said to Mary, “Woman, why are you crying? Who are you looking for?”
Just as he also asked those walking to Emmaus about the things that had happened to him, “What are these things you are saying to one another as you walk along the road?”
And just as he called to the apostles and asked them, “Little children, do you have any fish?” although he knew that they had caught nothing that night.
Just as he also asked them, “How many loaves do you have?”
Did the one who blessed the loaves and multiplied them not know how many there were?
Perhaps he also did not know who had touched the edge of his clothes, so that her blood stopped flowing?
Likewise, if the wickedness of your father Satan, or its fragments, reaches into you, O pagan, and fills you still more with unbelief,
I will say, acknowledging the truth, that he not only knows that she has been bleeding for twelve years, but he knows her from the time she was in her mother’s womb.
If a potter does not know the vessel he made with his own hands during his lifetime, Jesus himself knows those whom he formed in the beginning.
Those who know that [?]

[?] [?] the one who [?] fire and sulfur from heaven upon the people of Sodom and Gomorrah until he destroyed them because of their impiety, except for Lot and his children; the one who drowned Pharaoh and his multitude in the sea because of his godlessness.
Those who loved the curse, so that it would come upon them, said, “He cannot save himself from the hands of those who crucified him.”

The one who brought them all into existence; the one who made the earth open its mouth and swallow a multitude because they had sinned against him at that time, along with all those whom he destroyed in the wilderness.
These still more accursed people said, “If he is God, why did they crucify him?”
Who will be able to count the [?]
[?] all [?], just as a single one came forth from him and killed one hundred and eighty-five thousand people in a single night from the camp of multitudes of godless people.

And Moses, his chosen one, performed all these wonders in Egypt, in the Red Sea, and in the wilderness for forty years; and all the things he did through his servant Joshua son of Nun, who was mighty through his power.
And his servant Elijah raised the dead.
And he also divided the waters of the Jordan.
He walked on dry ground.
He also shut up the sky for three years and six months.
And he also brought fire down from heaven by calling upon the name of the Most High.

It consumed the [?], the water, the wood, and the calves slaughtered on them, which he had prepared as a representation of a sacrifice, and also the other ground, which he had made into a representation of a sea, together with everything around it.
And when he prayed, rainwater poured down upon the ground.
It yielded its fruit.
Likewise, his servant Elisha raised the dead.
And he struck the crowd [?].
which he did in the name of the Most High.
And the accursed people said, “It is not from God.”
So then, concerning these things, let us question the unbelievers, whose houses contain God's curse, and not in the presence of the believers, upon whose heads rests the Lord's blessing.
“Tell us, then, who is your god, you people who [?]?”
If you say, “Those in the sky are your gods,” you are cursed, because our Lord and our God—the God of us Christians—created them from the beginning to shine upon the earth.
And if you say of the calf and the cow and all the other animals that they are your gods, you are cursed, because the Lord of glory, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ
leaving them to pull the yoke, to cultivate the soil, to be eaten, to have their milk drunk, and to provide clothing from their wool.
If you say, “The wild animals are your gods,” you are even more accursed, because the Lord God commanded them all to come into being.
But if the dog and the cat are your gods, you are still more accursed, because the Lord God says, “I am he, I am he, and there is no other besides me.”
He assigned them their tasks: the one to keep watch, and the other to catch mice.

And if wood, stones, gold, silver, bronze, iron, and all the other things you worship are your gods, you are again more accursed, because the ruler of the whole world left them for us humans, knowing that we would take them for ourselves.
Do not [?] to say, “These godless people are cursed,” while listening to words spoken by good fathers: “You must not curse any person.”
Indeed, they are not even human beings.

But even if they are human beings, they are people who deserve to be cursed by those who say, “We are Christians,” because they have insulted the one who created them and have slandered the one who [?] them.

If it is right to curse the serpent, it is even more right to curse the children of that serpent, whom the Lord cursed from the beginning because he deceived Eve and caused Adam to stumble in paradise. In the same way, these cursed people now cause many to stumble and lead astray those who cannot recognize that they belong to Satan.
For this reason, if scripture says somewhere—or indeed if people of God say—“Do not curse anyone,” they mean, “Do not curse those who curse you,” as we said before.
They are not saying, “Do not curse the person who insults the one who gives you glory, Christ.”
But if the saints say, speaking about the tongue, “With it we curse people,” they mean that it is the foolishness of the person
who says, “I bless God,” while cursing good and faithful people against whom no one has anything to say.
This is how they said it: “My brothers, these things should not happen this way.”
And they are not saying, “You must not curse those who have wrapped themselves in the curse like a garment.”
And the curse entered them like water, and like oil into their bones.

If they say, “But Michael the archangel, when speaking with the devil and disputing with him about the body of Moses, did not dare to bring a slanderous judgment against him,” do not think they are saying, “You must not curse people who offer sacrifices to demons.”

As I heard, some of you said, “Michael certainly did not speak harsh words to the devil, but said, ‘May the Lord rebuke you.’” “In the same way,” they said, “it is not right to curse people who have come forth from Cronus.”
But the statement does not mean that the great archangel spared that devil by not cursing him.
This statement [?] now, “May the Lord rebuke you,” signifies even more strongly the curse that is coming upon him.
I will not hesitate to say that he is cursed, along with his pagan children.
He is all the more cursed along with them.
They are cursed along with him.
Or do you not see that this is not so?
What, then, is it but a curse and an insulting judgment?

Quite apart from what the Scriptures have said, ignorant, fruitless, and impure people are certainly indignant, because they say things they do not understand, like these other accursed people today who resemble them in blaspheming the greatness of God, because they do not know him or his works.
Listen now, so that we may understand that we alter the words the saints wrote, bringing them into line with our own desires and making them resemble us, because we do not want sound teaching.

And so that we may understand that they are speaking about people whom they compared to empty clouds driven along by the wind, and to dry, fruitless trees that have died a second time at their roots, and to violent waves of the sea casting up their shame, and to wandering stars for whom dense darkness has been prepared forever, because they dare to say things that are improper and that they do not understand.

You see that they do not find fault with those who pour curses down upon people who disbelieve everything written in the Scriptures—the things that the Lord God did, and the things that his saints did in his name.
So Scripture now says about them, “Likewise, these others, dreaming, defile their flesh, reject authority, and insult glorious beings.”
They rebuke the offspring of the ungodly at all times, down to these accursed people of today: “They insult things they do not understand.”
“But in the things they understand by animal instinct, they are destroyed.”
God of hosts, the Almighty, whose glory, wonders, and good gifts have filled the whole inhabited world.
Yet they reject him and blaspheme him.
But these accursed people are slaves to the crooked devil, whose wonders have filled the whole earth.
Through him they are destroyed in every kind of lawlessness.
The house of God, the church, which shines upon the whole earth and is filled with living words.
Their houses, however, which have become hosts to
demons and are filled with books of deception—through every kind of deceit they are destroyed in them.
But I return again to say that Satan is not the only one upon whom the great archangel Michael brings an insulting judgment, but also those who, through him, have fallen away from the straight path.

They also said that the angels did not bring an insulting judgment against them, just as they also wrote about the people who turned aside, became worthless, and followed the flesh, because they despised authority. They are bold and self-willed.
They do not tremble before glory, but speak insults, whereas the angels, who are greater in strength and power, do not bring an insulting judgment against them.
But these were born like irrational animals, to be captured and destroyed, slandering things they do not understand.

They will perish in their own destruction, being captured, having received the wages of injustice. They regard their daytime luxury as pleasure. They are insolent and filthy, living luxuriously and delighting in their deceptions, their eyes full of adultery.
And they do not stop sinning, deceiving those who are not firmly established. They have trained themselves—or rather their hearts—in acts of injustice. They are children of the curse.
I said again: Stop cursing those who have perished because of their foolishness. Stop bringing a slanderous judgment against them, or slandering them.

Therefore, when they say that the archangel Michael did not bring a slanderous judgment against them, and that the angels do not bring a slanderous judgment against these others, they are not sparing Satan and those who have followed them.
Who among those capable of killing a dragon that has killed many with its venom would spare it?
Rather, understand correctly what he uttered.

But this expression, “a slanderous judgment,” which he did not dare to bring against the devil or against the others who do his evil deeds, reveals a meaning like this: he did not dare to say, “If only the Lord God had never brought him into existence at all!”

If your destiny was to change in this way through your apostasy and become a devil, if only he had also not brought into existence the people who chose to act like animals—the pagans, the barbarians, and every godless heretic!

If only he would destroy you and his angels before the appointed time, pouring out all his anger upon you and fully unleashing all his wrath upon those who loved your alien voice and followed you rather than listening to the voice of the one who came into the world to rescue them, Jesus, and to save them from their godlessness!
This is the slanderous judgment that absolutely none of the children of God, from angels to human beings, will dare to pronounce.
Indeed, a thought of this kind belongs to grumbling people, who find fault with God without cause—God, whose goodness extends to all the things he has made.

Even if they changed and defiled themselves by their own choice, they did not dare to bring a slanderous judgment against them, as the pagans and heretics now dare to utter things that should not be said.
As many have said within my hearing: “Why did God create the devil?” And: [?]
[?] the Jews [?] not to happen to them [?] because he said, “Your house is left to you [?] your house is left to you yourselves [?].” [?] Instead of taking [?]
You will be trampled instead of straw; you will be given over to plunder instead of a brick; a curse will consume you instead of fire; and anger will destroy you instead of a sword.
For he is the one pursuing you. Jesus has not forgotten those whom you sent into his places, nor does he forget [?] the poor.
This evil rejoices over you, so that Christ will laugh at you and mock you, while you say, speaking about me, “He has gathered people around himself.”
[?] upon [?] stone, being submerged [?] while you accuse me before the rulers, or the authorities, or the laws.
Or do you not see how great the sin of these people is?
Have I, then, come [?] against the people for more than a year now? And to whom are they gathering, or who is gathering them?
Or what is this whole crowd doing on this mountain, except that God is calling them?
What did the God-loving count Chosroes—the man whom you could not discourage from coming to us—say?
He said, glorifying God, “You have made the desert a city.”
They themselves spoke differently, in [?], distorting the statement and telling lies.

It would have benefited you in both respects, O miserable people [?], according to the name by which you are called—not merely “Hyena,” but according to the character that the one who said these things saw in you—
not to let yourselves harden your hearts until all these sufferings come upon you, especially when you say [?]

As I heard that some of you said, “Michael did not utter any harsh words against the devil at all, but said, ‘May the Lord rebuke you.’ That is how it is,” they said: “One should not curse people who pour out libations to Cronus.”
But the statement does not mean that that great archangel spared the devil by not cursing him.
For this statement, “May the Lord rebuke you,” signifies even more strongly the curse coming upon him.
I will not hesitate to say that his pagan children curse me.
And he curses me along with them.
They curse me along with him.
Or do you not see that this is not so?
What, then, is a curse but a judgment against someone?

Not to mention what Scripture said, expressing indignation at ignorant, fruitless, and unclean people: they speak about things they do not understand, just like these others now who curse me and bring themselves to blaspheme the greatness of God, because they know neither him nor his works.
Listen now, so that we may understand that we distort the words the saints wrote, bending them to our own wishes, because we do not want sound teaching.

And so that we may understand that they are speaking about the people whom they compared to empty clouds driven by the wind, and to dry, fruitless trees that have died a second time in their roots, and to fierce waves of the sea spewing out their shame, and to wandering stars for whom thick darkness has been prepared forever, because they dare [?]
[?] the Lord God did, and the things his saints did in his name.
So they now said about them, “Likewise, these others, dreaming, defile their flesh, reject lordship, and blaspheme the glorious ones.”
Rebuking the offspring of the ungodly at all times, down to these people now who curse me, because they blaspheme what they do not know.
The things they know.
Make them walk groaning and weeping. You will make them, in turn, walk weeping and groaning.
Those who did not listen to them in their affliction—do not listen to them in their distress.

Those who did not have mercy on them—do not, in turn, have mercy on them, for your sake, Lord. And because of the tears of the poor, let them lie down in sorrow. You will judge those who oppress them, and you will fight against those who fight against them.
Those who made their deeds weigh heavily upon them with every suffering—you will repay their wickedness into their laps with every suffering.

[?] destroy their judgment. Do not forgive their sins. They too will come out disgraced when you judge them, because they have added to the suffering of widows, orphans, and strangers. [?] heart [?] mouth [?] and they stopped [?] wickedness [?] hear [?] righteous [?] righteous [?] people [?]

Therefore let them receive what is due to them and find no more.
Just as they made the poor beg, let the moneylender thoroughly search out everything they themselves possess.
Like those whom you cursed from the beginning through the mouths of those we have provoked, let the reproaches of those who reproach you come down upon them.

If they too acquire many houses, let them become deserted. Or if they already have large, beautiful houses, let there be no one living in them—as now there are many with no one living in them except slaves and cattle.
Therefore let them put this tablet of theirs [?] weeping [?].
A demon [?] his heart.
Who among you thought that you would give your strength to donkeys and let others saddle them for themselves?
Rather, your tablet, and others of this kind as well, and those who resemble them.
Where are your grand words and your accusations, with tricks and lies, against the one who seeks your welfare and who now establishes you in your life?
And let there be [?] for you [?] in the [?] judgment [?].

Disturbances, and you will be scattered from one end of the country to the other, so that a child will not find his father, nor a father his child, nor a man his wife, nor a woman her husband, to tell one another what is in their hearts or to comfort one another. Where could they do so? For your houses and your places will all become deserted in this way.
Where is the sound of joy and gladness that used to abound in them? For [?] too [?] inside [?].
[?] other livestock and every possession they found.
Whom have you spared, or on whom have you had pity, that those whom God has raised up against you, or into whose hands he has delivered you, should spare you or have pity on you?
For if anyone fears God, who repays each person according to their deeds starting here, even before they go to the place of full repayment, pay attention, and you will understand that no one [?].
Discourage him from coming to us. Say, what did he say as he gave glory to God? “You have turned a city into a wilderness.”
They themselves spoke [?] in another way, changing the statement and lying.

It would have benefited you on both counts, you miserable, savage people—not only according to the name you are called, “hyenas,” but also according to the character that the one saying these things saw in you.
So that you would not harden your hearts until all these sufferings come down upon you, especially as you say [?].
[?] says these things about those who oppose his thoughts at all times.
Nor are the good words that some people will address to us better than those that Jesus, our king and our Lord, speaks into our hearts at all times.
Nor would the battle against those who oppose us be greater than the battle against their father Satan, whom we fight at all times.
If the help of brothers and friends who help one another is good—for it is good when a person finds faithful friends and true brothers—God’s help is nevertheless greater than all these.
Therefore I was not concerned [?] with these or those others.
Did not [?], a pagan duke, dare to say, when he came here, “I was indeed amazed that you are strong”?
I said to him, “Why would those who have no God as their master not be happy?”
Do they not worship things made by hand—idols of demons?
Like those about whom the prophet said, “There is no joy for the ungodly,” says the Lord God.
Woe to you! Woe to you, assembly of calves and dogs and every wild beast, sister of the one from whom God's anger has not departed, down to this day and until the end!
For an assembly of calves and dogs surrounded me and seized me.
Ungrateful one, you are not hidden from Jesus, nor does he forget you, because they insult him and his saints within you or through you.
They have already explained their name: “She who is full of demons, whom every evil spirit has clothed [?] lying to God.”
What will you do on the day of their rebuke?
Or will you laugh at yourself?
For they insult God and revile his saints, while you listen
as they speak insolently against God and his people, not in private rooms but in marketplaces and streets, where many people hear.
I too say it openly in the midst of this crowd, so that the [?] of the districts and the whole land may hear:
“Cursed are those who say, ‘Gods can be crucified,’ or, ‘A god can die.’”
Cursed are those who say, “If God is a god, why did he not know where the devil had come from?”
They said this because they heard in Job the King, the Lord God Almighty, asking that demon, “From [?]”
[?] speaks like a human being in the Scriptures.
For if those godless people had understood that it is people's custom to threaten wicked slaves and to say, “Where are you coming from?” even when they know
Just as Elisha questioned Gehazi, knowing where he had come from and what he had done, so the Lord questioned the devil threateningly,
“Where are you coming from, destroyer, you who boast over weak people?
Have you then considered my servant Job, weakling? There is no one like him.
If you want to fight, turn toward him.
For I have tolerated you, demon, to test my chosen ones, so that they may laugh at you through everything you seek from them, when they defeat you, the angel who is put to death by those who ask [?]
